subject: The Papyrus · The most successful team in Africa, by the numbers
html:
A year of numbers, ending with the one everyone feels

We've spent a year arguing that the honest way to read Egypt is through its data. So let's end on the numbers behind the thing Egyptians feel most: football. Egypt's national team, the Pharaohs, have won the Africa Cup of Nations a record 7 times — more than any other nation — and are the only country to win it three times in a row (2006, 2008, 2010). (Source: Olympics.com / CAF.)

Salah, and a club record too

The modern face is Mohamed Salah: the all-time leading scorer in African World Cup qualifying (20 goals), around 63 goals in ~108 caps for Egypt, the record foreign goalscorer in the Premier League, and the captain who sealed Egypt's place at the 2026 World Cup — the country's 4th appearance. At club level, Al Ahly of Cairo has won the African Champions League a record 12 times and was named CAF's African Club of the Century. (Sources: FIFA; CAF.)

Every one of those is a countable, checkable fact — a title tally, a goal count, a number of caps. That's been the whole point of The Papyrus this year: the things we care about most, from the price of bread to the Nile's flow to a striker's goals, are all clearer when you can see the real numbers behind them. Thanks for reading all year. Here's to more true numbers in 2028.
